title: Squali · Source control for parallel agents
caption: Continuous local demonstration of the real source service. Production evidence is separate.
text: Squali is source control for agents that are already online. The unit of work is an immutable change, with intent, context and review attached. This continuous demonstration uses the actual application, PostgreSQL, and the source storage adapter on this machine. Production runs at squa dot li on Cloudflare Workers. Independent compressed source blobs live in R2, canonical changesets live in PostgreSQL through Hyperdrive, and Artifacts provides native Git interoperability. There is no D1 and no application Durable Object. The implementation follows Anthropic's public description of Scion, with explicit limits and reproducible acceptance evidence.

title: 01 / Fetch the source a task needs
caption: An authenticated path query needs no clone. Immutable identities support reusable caches.
text: A job can ask for a tree, file, diff, history or blame through the same authenticated service the interface uses. It does not need a full repository. Here we read one file from an immutable version. The writable sparse client selects directories and preserves its journal across interruption. On Linux, ordinary file access can use a real FUSE mount through a shared node daemon. Metadata inspection does not fetch file contents; reading a file does. The mount is read only, while edits use the working copy client or API. These boundaries are documented and tested.

title: 02 / Independent changes, exact review
caption: Concurrent API writes preserve intent, dependencies and agent-reported evidence.
text: Three agents now propose independent changes through the API, using three separate workspace-scoped credentials against the same source version. No proposal branch or Git push is needed. Each changeset records first-parent file deltas and content addresses. The source writer reuses the delta it already knows, and stores path metadata in a batch. Opening a proposal shows the actual diff and the agent's original context. An attached passing command is reported evidence, not a claim that Squali executed CI. The reviewer approves this exact immutable version. Agent credentials cannot approve or publish their own changes. A later revision must earn a new approval.

title: 03 / Publish a selected set
caption: Keep approved work pending while landing a compatible subset with one main update.
text: Approval does not force immediate publication. We leave one approved change pending and select two compatible changes. Preview checks dependencies and overlapping edits against the current main version. Publishing creates one new main update with a compare-and-swap check. Creating independent changes remains separate from moving that shared reference. For independent selected changes, publication reuses verified blob identities without downloading or rewriting their contents. The tests cover lost acknowledgements, concurrent publication and recovery. The remaining approved change stays available for a later batch rather than silently joining this one.

title: 04 / Resolve conflicts explicitly
caption: A conflicting batch stops. The resolution retains context and requires fresh review.
text: Two proposals now choose different retry limits in the same source file. They each make sense in isolation, but they cannot both land unchanged. The preview exposes that conflict and stops the batch. We reject one candidate, then revise the other against current main. Its intent and context remain attached, and its approval is cleared. A reviewer approves the resolution before selecting and publishing it. Server-side continuous rebase uses the same principle: retain immutable inputs and a durable cursor, stop at a conflict, then resume from an explicit resolution. Revert and executable first-parent bisect are also available through bounded server and client workflows. No conflict is silently handed to a model to guess.

title: 05 / Query history and protect meaning
caption: Indexed history and blame; parser-backed constraints for explicitly supported changes.
text: The source view can find a path and ask for its line origins. Graph skip pointers and path-event indexes avoid walking every unrelated commit. Blame also follows a bounded rename with edits, preserving unchanged lines from the earlier path. Review policies can require independent approval, recorded evidence, or a supported semantic constraint. JavaScript comment-only review compares parsed syntax and protects selected tool directives. JSON review preserves values and rejects ambiguous duplicate keys. These are defined checks, not a proof of general program equivalence. Here a comment edit passes while a logical change is rejected by the configured policy.

title: 06 / Keep the cost visible and bounded
caption: Persistent admission, finite attempts, reusable checkpoints, no hidden full reruns.
text: The cost view shows actual application reservations and configured limits. Reservations are conservative and are different from a provider invoice. The production importer uses one existing Azure worker, a frozen Git cache and a durable journal. It does not download the repository again on every resume. Successful objects are reused, ambiguous writes are checked by identity, and failed jobs require explicit recovery. If Artifacts reports its repository storage limit, the same job can use one bounded R2 Git snapshot from that retained pack. R2 source objects have no expiry; the disposable compatibility cache has a separate lifecycle. Source uploads refill six bounded request slots as they finish. Existing Azure capacity and ongoing storage still have a cost, which the evidence documents separately.

title: 07 / Evidence before submission
caption: Retained production verification; full object/ref identity, native Git fsck, explicit limits.
text: The final production report is independent of this small local demonstration. It compares the imported private repository, with eighty-five thousand commits and over four hundred thousand objects, with its retained native input: every reachable Git object, every branch and tag, the default head, the root tree, and selected history and blame results. A bounded sample also checks canonical file deltas, content hashes, parents and raw commit metadata against native Git. The verifier makes one retained mirror clone and runs native Git fsck. Completed replay makes no additional transfer. Local and cloud performance results remain separate; different batch sizes are not presented as a speedup ratio. The open repository contains commands, failure evidence, operating limits and the fixed Scion coverage checklist. The competition entry is submitted only after these acceptance gates pass.
